historical_context.time_period: Identity Crisis era, 2478, during early implementation of the Ganymede Route Compact
historical_context.location: Registry Annex B in a Ganymede orbital dock, a converted convoy dispatch bay with one shared wet/dry route-voice desk; the annex, cast, convoy, and docket are fixture-local dramatization.
historical_context.summary: A routine route-voice signing for a Lightsail Express convoy becomes a scope dispute when the translation buffer turns a navigator's two-watch mandate into broad operational consent. An immediate collision warning then tests whether a one-cycle safety hold can remain distinct from permanent route authority.

public_facts.text: The 2478 Compact established route-steward representation, shared hazard ledgers, rescue obligations, and legal status for navigator councils in convoy arbitration.
A route-voice mandate names its steward, alternate, represented crews and segment, permitted acts, exclusions, and expiry; witnesses attest source and scope rather than choosing the speaker.
A declared alternate must answer through the recorded channel, and silence does not transfer navigator voice to an employer.
An affected navigator may issue a one-decision-cycle safety hold without letting the emergency act settle the disputed mandate.
Lightsail Express relies on predictable movement and Navigator corridor reputation to move bulk goods, data, and people.
Ganymede's route authority overlaps with carrier, insurer, dock labor, research, and industrial interests rather than replacing them with one sovereign office.

ambient_pressures.text: Every minute spent repairing voice access consumes berth time, wages, fuel margin, cargo life, and bond capacity.
A clean translation can make a contested uplift signal easier to insure while demoting the source voice into an attachment.
Dock labor duplicate custody offers a small defense because it preserves the source outside the carrier and insurer offices that benefit from broad wording.

groups.label: Compact-recognized navigator watch
institutional_logic: Turn indispensable navigation labor, shared hazard knowledge, and rescue practice into scoped corridor authority.
material_incentives: Preserve route access and rescue capacity
Avoid delays that make small crews surrender scope
internal_shames: Using translation fluency as proof of consent
prestige_markers: Refusals that keep a corridor usable
emotional_display_norms: Disagreement is made operational through source signals, scope fields, refusal, and withdrawal rather than performed for dryside sympathy.
trust_defaults: Trusts navigator-controlled channels and witnessed duplicate records; treats carrier urgency and insurer legibility as interests, not neutral facts.
speech_register_cues: Acoustic and pressure signal paired with dryside notation

groups.label: Ganymede dock labor syndicate recorders
institutional_logic: Witness source, channel, scope, and expiry without becoming the represented voice.
material_incentives: Avoid making every accommodation cost a worker's job
internal_virtues: Knowing which office owns which act
internal_shames: Letting a clean form replace a living source
Inventing authority to save a schedule
prestige_markers: A stoppage with a named cause
taboo_triggers: Asking a recorder to choose the steward
Hiding schedule pressure inside neutral interface text
emotional_display_norms: Humor and procedural dryness make conflict bearable; fear becomes a hold, duplicate, named requester, or refusal to sign.
trust_defaults: Trusts source receipts and other workers' custody more than carrier-owned translation defaults.
speech_register_cues: Short questions about source and scope

groups.label: Lightsail Express convoy dispatch
institutional_logic: Turn recognized route decisions into predictable bulk movement across low-trust corridors.
internal_virtues: A route commitment other carriers honor
internal_shames: A promise that cannot be scheduled
taboo_triggers: A mandate too narrow to launch
Procedure that consumes a cargo window
emotional_display_norms: Anxiety appears as clock watching, compressed phrasing, and requests for one usable sentence.
trust_defaults: Trusts navigator competence and accepted Compact records while preferring scope broad enough to keep operations moving.

groups.label: Jovian convoy insurers
institutional_logic: Convert witnessed authority and route risk into a price the convoy system will accept.
internal_shames: A policy resting on an unusable signal
A challenge that makes prior coverage incoherent
taboo_triggers: Source channels no desk can read
emotional_display_norms: Concern appears as price color, attachment status, and a request for a cleaner governing sentence.
trust_defaults: Trusts standardized translations and witnessed mandates; may mistake legibility for faithful representation.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: A navigator watch needs its decisions to bind convoy operations without letting an employer own the channel through which those decisions become legible.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Keep navigator speech scoped by route, interval, named act, source signal, and expiry; never treat employment, translation, or availability as voice transfer.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: The recorder can make a navigator's mandate usable or unusable but cannot choose the steward or enlarge the mandate.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Player choices should operate on witness, copy, pause, annotation, and refusal surfaces instead of puppeting navigator consent.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: Accurate scope and accessible replay consume scarce berth time, cargo life, wages, and coverage margin, making procedural perfection easier for wealthy operators.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Every repair or refusal must leave a clock, cargo, wage, bond, or trust consequence visible.

observer_read: A costly limit on operational flexibility
target_self_read: Author of one bounded route commitment
Holder of rescue and refusal obligations
misread_patterns: Treats a safety hold as proof of broad authority
Treats a ready alternate as replaceable capacity
Treats an exclusion as needless friction
factional_misread_matrix.projection_use: Let dispatcher pressure remain locally rational and materially useful while showing where schedule language expands voice.

observer_read: A risk-bearing authority only when translated into portable clauses
A source signal that needs office adoption
target_self_read: The principal whose exact signal and limits the office is meant to carry
misread_patterns: Treats accessible source replay as an optional service cost
factional_misread_matrix.projection_use: Use insurer language to expose how representation can be preserved in storage while displaced from governing authority.

observer_read: A worker office that can still choose convenience
misread_patterns: May read a careful non-signature as erasure
May overestimate how much a union copy can stop after departure
factional_misread_matrix.projection_use: Keep trust conditional on what the recorder materially preserves, not on stated sympathy.

role_pressure_fields.summary: A union recorder who can witness source and scope, operate the shared board, preserve a duplicate, pause or withhold a signature, and record an emergency hold without choosing the navigator speaker.
A navigator chosen by the affected watch to bind named route acts for a named interval through a recorded source channel.
failure_modes: A safety hold reused as general consent

role_pressure_fields.summary: A Lightsail worker responsible for getting perishable and life-support cargo through a narrowing departure slot under recognized route authority.
failure_modes: Converting emergency competence into permanent authority

role_pressure_fields.summary: An insurer clerk who can price and clear coverage against a witnessed mandate but cannot choose the navigator steward or settle a voice challenge.
failure_modes: Pricing the translation instead of the source
Treating dissent as harmless because it remains attached
Making access failure the navigator's cost

known_context.text: Sen knows the local board, translation buffer, union press, witness rule, berth clock, declared steward and alternate, and observable route and bond pressure.

beliefs.text: Sen believes a useful record must say whose voice, which act, and until when, but also knows delay can harm crews and cargo.

misreads.text: Sen may mistake visible dissent or an independent copy for effective redress after a broad authorization already governs.

must_not_know.text: Sen must not know Talu's private appraisal, insurer decisions outside the displayed bond field, or how later Navigator institutions develop.

known_context.text: Talu knows their watch's source mandate, route segment, powers, exclusions, expiry, alternate, immediate hazard, and the room's visible translation divergence.

beliefs.text: Talu treats translation as an instrument and refuses to let emergency competence authorize acts the watch did not delegate.

misreads.text: Talu may read Sen's refusal to witness an emergency hold as dryside erasure even when Sen intends to preserve the mandate challenge.

must_not_know.text: Talu must not know private insurer pricing logic beyond the displayed field or treat the 2478 procedure as the mature later coalition's settled doctrine.

known_context.text: Rem knows the cargo, departure throat, crew schedule, route requirement, displayed translation, and whether the witness square has cleared.

beliefs.text: Rem believes a route decision has to become portable operational language before a convoy can rely on it.

misreads.text: Rem may mistake a bounded safety hold for proof of broad route authority because both produce the necessary safe movement.

must_not_know.text: Rem must not know Talu's interior consent or treat carrier dependency as ownership of navigator judgment.

known_context.text: Vela knows the bond terms, accepted witness fields, displayed authority, attachments, and price changes visible from the insurer desk.

beliefs.text: Vela believes portable wording protects the convoy system from ambiguous authority and loss.

misreads.text: Vela may treat faithful source preservation as sufficient even when the source has been demoted beneath governing translation.

must_not_know.text: Vela must not decide who speaks for the navigator watch or claim insurer adoption creates corridor authority.

author_only_boundaries.text: Registry Annex B, Sen, Talu, Pel, Rem, Vela, Common Wake, the ore lighter, and this specific docket are fixture-local dramatization, not added historical canon.

The mature Route Choir, Waystation Council, Corridor Court, and Rescue Ledger system is later institutional context; participants in this 2478 scene should not speak as if its full later form already exists.

open_questions.notes: The fixture uses one bottlenose-dolphin body as local dramatization because later Navigator examples support that lineage; it does not claim exclusivity or founding primacy.

open_questions.question: What exact hardware implemented navigator-controlled source channels in 2478?
open_questions.notes: The fixture uses a local multimodal board, waterborne pressure pulses, low sound, light, raised pins, and a dry translation buffer, following later Navigator interface doctrine without canonizing one universal device.
